questions.title: What to do if you move your ball by mistake while looking for it
questions.question: You are looking for your ball in the long grass. Your foot moves the ball by accident. What should you do?

choices.text: Hit the ball from where it stopped
Put the ball back where it was with no penalty
Put the ball back and add one penalty shot
Drop a new ball and keep playing

questions.explanation: If you move your golf ball by mistake when you are looking for it, just put it back where it was. You do not have to count a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra shots you must add to your score if you break a rule.
The area with long grass next to the short grass (fairway) on a golf course.

questions.teachingTip: Show children how to look for a ball in long grass using a club or gently moving grass with a foot, reminding them to watch where the ball is.
likelyMisconceptions: Some might think they have to play the ball from the new spot. Remind them the ball must go back to where it was.
Some might think they get a penalty every time the ball moves. Explain there is no penalty if it only moves while you are trying to find it.

questions.title: Ball moved while looking for it
questions.question: If you accidentally move your ball while searching for it in the rough, what should you do according to the rules?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it ends up
Replace the ball and take a one-stroke penalty
Drop a new ball and play on

questions.explanation: If your ball is accidentally moved while searching for it, you must put it back without penalty.
